reason: Oil-spill containment is useful environmental content, but the matched uses facet is incidental: it does not identify a useful everyday mixture or teach one of the current separation core facets.
shaped bowl makes solid clay useful as a floating object; EN/TL/BIS preserve the shape comparison.
Identifies downward weight opposed by upward buoyancy in a floating object, a concrete gravity-effect component; the force balance is preserved in both translations.
The candle itself does lose mass in an open system; the answer says no without defining the larger conserved system. Needs wording correction before conservation-of-mass core use.

Coal is rendered uling in both translations, conflating mined fossil coal with charcoal; the English also describes stored carbon as already stored carbon dioxide. Correct before carbon-cycle recovery.
Complete combustion products depend on fuel composition; all fuel does not necessarily produce both carbon dioxide and water. Needs hydrocarbon-fuel qualification.
Fresh air alone does not guarantee continued burning: fuel and adequate heat also matter. The statement makes oxygen arrival the sole continuation condition and needs qualification.
Explains oxygen consumption in combustion as a chemical reaction; the eating metaphor is identifiable in all three versions and no experiment is instructed.
Cebuano translates caterpillar as tangkong, a plant/vegetable term, breaking the life-stage sequence. English and Tagalog are useful but the shared card needs translation repair.
Butterfly pupae may use silk attachment and not all moths make silk cocoons. The absolute no-silk versus silk distinction is false; Smithsonian butterfly anatomy describes silk pads/slings.
Gives the complete egg, caterpillar, pupa, adult sequence in all languages; valid life-cycle content without requiring a flowchart on every fact.
Correct four-stage butterfly sequence retained in TL and Cebuano; teaches the butterfly comparison component rather than a chart-making activity.
Identifies a butterfly as an insect with six legs, a real classification feature, in all languages. Adult anatomy is implicit in the winged butterfly example.

Specifies most butterflies and the adult stage, avoiding an all-species lifespan claim; both translations preserve those limits. Adult duration supports life-cycle comparison. Verified against https://www.amnh.org/exhibitions/butterflies/butterfly-faq .
Both translations replace the chrysalis stage with supot (bag), while English names the pupa/chrysalis. The intended technical stage needs a clearer localized label before approval.
All languages distinguish the egg, larva, pupa and mature butterfly; useful complete-metamorphosis teaching component.
Cebuano translates related as managhigala (friends), losing the biological relationship; English teaching value is clear but localization needs correction.
Names a familiar useful drink made by combining calamansi juice, water and sugar; an everyday mixture example, not a claim that every drink is uniform. Translations retain ingredients and use.
Translations turn calcium-rich food into eating calcium itself, losing the food qualification. Digestive/air matches are incidental to bone repair.
Chalk and bones are not made of the same mineral: calcium carbonate/gypsum differs from bone hydroxyapatite. Shared calcium does not establish mineral identity.
TL/BIS say vitamin D is obtained from sunlight rather than synthesized in skin; the explicit skin-production mechanism is lost. Needs correction before absorption teaching.
Callisto geology is not observation of objects commonly visible in the day/night sky. The moon regex matches a remote Jovian satellite rather than the intended observable Moon.
The old classification-table match came from grows. Current flowering core requires a seed/fruit link, which this flower-description card lacks; no current appropriate core facet admits it.
Cebuano question Giunsa pagpuyo sa camouflage asks about living/residing rather than how camouflage works. Hold for language repair despite a sound English explanation.
Historical candle-clock use is not connected to home/local-community invention impact; the uses keyword alone is insufficient for the proposed core competency.
A candle extinguishes before oxygen reaches zero; the card states all oxygen is used up and directly invites an unsupervised flame experiment. Needs corrected demonstration framing.
Oxygen concentration becomes insufficient for combustion before all oxygen is used up. The stated closed-jar mechanism requires qualification and safe demonstration framing.
Directly instructs holding a spoon over a flame without adult supervision, and simplifies soot formation as unburned carbon carried in smoke. Needs a reviewed demonstration version.
Distinguishes physical wax melting from chemical burning in a candle; both translations preserve the two changes and their classifications.
Explains removal of water from cane juice by evaporation to concentrate syrup; substantive separation technique, with process and result retained in TL/BIS.
Tagalog uses pantal for flat teeth (a rash/welt term), while the English description also treats front and back teeth too uniformly as flat. Correct the anatomy wording and translation.
Human canines are the subject, whereas the matched G3 facet is observation of animal external feeding structures. Current human digestion mouth pattern does not admit this short version.
Wick is translated piti in both languages rather than a clear wick term; vaporization is omitted. Hold for localization repair of the mechanism.
Macroscopic pores/tubes are not spaces between particles. The current particle-spaces match is incidental, and plant water transport is oversimplified as capillarity alone.
Explicitly contrasts upward water movement with downward gravity; supports observing gravity effects without claiming gravity is absent. TL/BIS retain both directions.
Water supply to cut flowers also depends on transpiration-driven xylem flow; the habitat water match does not classify an aquatic organism. Needs a corrected transport mapping.
Describes the concave water meniscus at glass edges, a necessary volume-reading feature; no false eye-level credit. Both translations retain curved surface and adhesion.
Narrower tubes do not have a greater total upward surface-tension force; rise depends on force relative to liquid weight. The explanation confuses pressure/height with stronger total force.
Gaps between paper fibers are macroscopic pore spaces, not the between-particle spaces in G7-M-3. Sound absorbency example needs a different core mapping.
Pores in paper/cloth are not the particle-model spaces in the candidate competency. Do not restore based on the incidental word spaces.
Ruminant regurgitation is not the human digestive-tract route taught by this lesson; a carabao example would need an explicit comparative facet, not a chew keyword.
G4-L-1 is explicitly human body systems. Carabao digestive fermentation cannot be substituted for human stomach function merely because digest matches.
The human digestive-system stomach facet must not be filled with a four-chamber ruminant stomach card; risks teaching the wrong anatomy.

The mineral-seeking explanation for carabao soil licking needs a species-specific source before attributing the behavior. Retain for verification rather than infer solely from an environmental-needs match.
Contrasts milk feeding in a young calf with later grass eating, a concrete mammal-development comparison. TL/BIS preserve the developmental sequence.
Cheese is a biotechnology keyword, but this card never establishes fermentation or the production process; not enough for the traditional-fermentation core facet.
Age-related pale patches on carabao bodies are not verified here and could have other causes. Do not use as a generic mammal-development fact without evidence.
Links milk production explicitly to the mammal group using a familiar carabao; translations retain the defining feature and example.
Uses sparse hair on a carabao as a mammalian classification feature; both translations retain the comparison with other mammals and dog fur.
Horns are not a shared diagnostic mammalian trait, and no comparative classification is explained; this defense/body-part fact needs a better facet than the mammal word alone.
Explains warm-blooded mammalian temperature regulation through the carabao example; TL/BIS retain the elementary steady-temperature meaning rather than cold blood as a literal label.
Identifies bacterial multiplication in warm milk as a characteristic action of the bacteria group; translations preserve organism, growth and spoilage relationship.
Milk surplus beyond every calf requirement is not guaranteed for all mothers; the never-hungry assertion depends on production and husbandry. Needs qualification.

Explicitly connects mammal classification to mothers producing milk for calves; both translations retain offspring feeding and collection of extra milk, without the never-hungry guarantee in another card.
Translations omit often and imply cheese/yogurt can always be tolerated; dairy tolerance varies. Correct the qualified health claim before use.
Provides carabao and goat examples sharing mammalian milk production; translations preserve the group comparison and correct the cows-only misconception.
The purported official national-animal distinction needs authoritative verification. Also land is matched inside island, not a terrestrial habitat classification.
A carabao pulling a plow is a concrete example of pull causing motion in familiar farm work; translations retain the load and pulling action.
Swimming ability does not classify a carabao as aquatic. Placing this in the aquatic habitat core would reinforce a habitat misconception.
Preference for wallowing does not explain water as a universal survival need; the matched water word is not sufficient for basic-needs core teaching.
Dietary fiber can be fermented by gut microbes; the unqualified not-digested/no-energy framing needs a more precise human-enzyme distinction before digestive teaching.
Hunger does not mean all glucose energy is used up, and eating carbohydrates does not universally resolve dizziness/weakness. Correct the medical causal claim.
Traces sunlight into carbohydrate made by a rice plant and then eaten by a person, an explicit producer-to-consumer energy-transfer example. Both translations retain this transfer.
Describes starch breakdown and rising glucose but does not explain homeostatic regulation; translations also render chemical digestion as physical crushing. Needs repair/remapping.

Remap from electricity to atomic identity: carbon atomic number six means six protons; neutrality gives six electrons. Both translations preserve numbers and neutrality. Carbon identity checked against https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/6/Carbon .
Identifies living organisms as containing carbon, a biotic-reservoir component of the carbon cycle; both translations retain element and living-things scope.
Four carbon bonds does not explain valence electrons in the outer shell. It matches bond but lacks the concept required by G9-M-3; no suitable precise core mapping recorded.
Never created or destroyed is unqualified across all processes, rather than scoped to ordinary carbon cycling; should not become a universal atom-conservation claim.

Connects tree/ocean uptake with human disruption of carbon balance; translations preserve the present imbalance. Consistent with NASA carbon-cycle account: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/the-carbon-cycle/ .
Says the cycle keeps everything balanced without the current human-emissions imbalance or an undisturbed-system qualification. Prefer the qualified card in this same batch.
Directly defines carbon movement through living organisms and environmental reservoirs; full reservoir list and recurring movement preserved in both translations.

Names photosynthesis, breathing and decay as carbon-transfer processes across living and environmental reservoirs; translations preserve all three processes. Conservation phrasing is situated in the carbon-cycle context.
CO2 density is conditional on temperature and mixing, and extinguishers also cool; the always-sinks explanation is an overgeneralized fire-safety mechanism needing revision.
Remap to air mixture: explicitly identifies carbon dioxide as a small atmospheric gas component and describes its plant/heat roles; both translations preserve these properties.
Translations call carbon the principal element composing bodies, which can imply most abundant by mass (oxygen is). Use the explicitly a-main-building-block version instead.

Identifies carbon by name as an element present in living things; supports first-ten element recognition without claiming the card itself teaches its symbol. TL/BIS preserve that it is a main component, not the only one.

Contrasts biological fast and geological slow carbon cycling; translations preserve the two reservoir groups. Verified against NASA fast/slow cycle explanation: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/the-carbon-cycle/ .
Explicitly shows carbon transferred through feeding from organisms into animal bodies; both translations preserve plant and animal food sources.
Both translations render coal as uling, conflating fossil coal with charcoal. Repair fuel names before restoring this fossil-formation card.
Carbon does not simply melt at 3550 C under ordinary pressure; sublimation/pressure and allotrope distinctions are missing. The stated diamond melting fact is unreliable.

Names carbon as the atomic framework in familiar biological molecules, an element-recognition example; translations preserve molecules containing carbon with other atoms rather than calling sugar pure elemental carbon.
Activated-carbon removal mainly involves adsorption, not just tiny holes mechanically filtering everything; the card collapses mechanisms and needs clearer separation teaching.
Explains long-term storage of biological carbon in fossil fuel before its modern combustion; translations retain buried organisms, time and fuel formation. Geological storage is a cycle component.

Identifies carbon with a meaningful approximate body-mass abundance example; TL/BIS preserve second rank and roughly one fifth. NIH lists carbon at 18.5 percent by mass: https://nigms.nih.gov/biobeat/2015/07/elements-that-keep-us-alive-also-give-color-to-fireworks .
Pencil lead normally includes graphite and clay, and charcoal is not pure carbon. The English made-of claim needs a contains qualifier before elemental-material examples.
Sugar and proteins are compounds containing carbon, not forms of elemental carbon. The statement conflates allotropes with carbon compounds.
Explains repeated reuse of carbon atoms across living organisms and presents dinosaur history as a possibility; TL/BIS preserve the recurring-cycle concept and tentative dinosaur example.
Compares named elements carbon and oxygen through structural and respiration roles; translations retain the quoted burning metaphor and distinguish food-derived carbon from inhaled oxygen.
Carbon-chain bonding detail does not explain the particle-model claim about a distinct particle kind for each pure substance; atom keyword alone is insufficient.
Traces dietary body carbon back through plants to air, a concise biological carbon-cycle pathway; both translations retain that sequence.
Plankton includes nonphotosynthetic organisms; the photosynthesis claim needs phytoplankton or photosynthetic plankton qualification in all languages.

Identifies carbonate rocks as the major geological carbon store and links shells/coral to long residence; TL/BIS preserve reservoir and timescale. Supported by https://www.energy.gov/science/doe-explainsthe-carbon-cycle .
Shells are structures rather than organisms, and corals build skeletons rather than shells. Needs clearer animal/skeleton wording before the carbonate pathway is taught.
A sink must absorb more carbon than it releases over a period, whereas storing carbon alone defines a reservoir. Add the net-uptake distinction.

Links decaying organisms to soil carbon storage and compares the soil reservoir with atmosphere; translations preserve both relationships. NASA reservoir account supports the comparison: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/the-carbon-cycle/ .
Storage is presented as one fixed step in a single ordered loop forever; carbon pathways branch and have different residence times. Needs less deterministic cycle wording.
